transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Ward (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Partnerships), Alex Rivera (Solaris Head of Partnerships), Priya Nair (Solaris Infra), Mark Delaney (Solaris CTO), Sofia Morales (Solaris Product)

Summary:
Quick intro between Redwood and SolarisCloud to evaluate partnership for co-located GPU offering + integrations (marketplace, private deployment options). Discussed technical fit (A100/H100), networking (VPC peering, private link), compliance (SOC2, KMS), and an initial pilot/benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Partnership model (resell vs integration)
- Technical integration points: private deployment, VPC peering, on-prem options, API integration
- Benchmark plan (latency/throughput, model variants)
- Security/compliance checklist and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Ward: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um i'm ethan from redwood, i'm the AE on this motion. maya my SE is here, she'll run through technicals. quick round of intros?
[00:18] Alex Rivera: yeah alex here, head of partnerships at solariscloud. we run the marketplace and partner program. happy to explore both reseller and deeper infra integrations.
[00:25] Priya Nair: priya infra, i'll own the bench and network stuff, especially peering and egress.
[00:30] Mark Delaney: mark, cto. interested in how this would run on our bare-metal fleet — want predictable latency and cost.
[00:36] Maya Chen: thanks, quick overview: redwood is an inference platform — hosted api, dedicated pools, and private (vpc/on-prem) deployments. our runtime does batching, prefix/kv cache, and quantization paths. we optimize kernels based on arch and seq len.
[00:52] Mark Delaney: when you say "dedicated" — that's reserved gpu pools? like a tenant gets an entire node?
[00:58] Maya Chen: yes, dedicated is reserved capacity with SLA targets. you can configure autoscale and burst. we also support private deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed in a vpc and the inference runtime runs on your infra.
[01:10] Priya Nair: ok so two options — we could 1) put Redwood Dedicated onto our infra as a managed partner offering or 2) let customers use Redwood hosted endpoints w/ hybrid routing. what are typical tradeoffs?
[01:23] Maya Chen: tradeoff is cost vs control. hosted is fastest to onboard but egress/data residency and compliance might be concerns; private gives you direct network control and kms/hsm integration. dedicated pools lower latency jitter but cost is higher vs multi-tenant. caching + batching reduce per-token cost substantially if workloads are predictable.
[01:42] Ethan Ward: and from a GTM perspective we see partners do a marketplace listing first (hosted integration) then a private/dedicated option for enterprise customers.
[01:52] Alex Rivera: hm makes sense. on the infra side — we run a mix of A100 and H100 nodes across regions. Priya — i'll let you fill in more.
[02:00] Priya Nair: yes we have A100 40GB and H100 80GB across eu/us. network-wise we allow VPC peering and private link but some customers need air-gapped. latency is often our ask, we target <40ms p50 for short completion inference.
[02:17] Maya Chen: good. for <40ms p50 we typically recommend model sharding, pinned instances (dedicated), and locality — routing requests to the nearest pool. we also do KV cache to avoid recomputing prefixes which helps latency for chat use-cases.
[02:31] Mark Delaney: how much of that is in prod today? curious about kernel selection for H100 vs A100.
[02:36] Maya Chen: our runtime picks kernels based on model arch and seq length heuristics; we've tuned for common open models and have verified profiles. that said we sometimes see perf delta between H100 and A100 depending on model and batch size — we'll run model-specific benchmarks.
[02:52] Alex Rivera: ok would you be open to a joint benchmark running on our infra? we want Redwood to demo on our A100/H100 fleet, show latency and throughput, cost-per-token estimates — then decide whether to list as managed offering.
[03:03] Ethan Ward: absolutely. that's what we do with GPU partners. maya — we should propose a minimal bench.
[03:08] Maya Chen: suggest: 1) pick 2 model sizes (e.g., 7B and 70B quantized variant), 2) run p50/p95 latency tests at varied concurrency and batch sizes, 3) measure tokens/sec and cost and memory usage. we'll bring our test harness (small python runner + tracing).
[03:27] Priya Nair: that sounds fine. we'll need detail on network ports, expected kernel driver versions, and root access assumptions. we don't want to open extra privileges.
[03:36] Maya Chen: understood. for private deployments we run as non-root and integrate with your k8s/nomad/DCOS as required; we can also run a fully air-gapped package if needed. we'll send requirements.
[03:47] Mark Delaney: security — SOC 2, sso, audit logs, KMS. do you have SOC2? can you do customer-managed keys?
[03:55] Ethan Ward: redwood is SOC 2 compliant. for private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and we can surface audit logs for inference requests. i'll send the security pack.
[04:06] Alex Rivera: competitors — we've seen calls from astrascale and titangrid — they push appliance-first stories. what's unique about redwood?
[04:15] Maya Chen: focus on production-grade inference with developer UX: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, built-in routing/fallbacks, cost controls (batching, caching, quantization recs), and strong observability. we also do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity is constrained.
[04:33] Sofia Morales: curious about pricing — do you price per-token on marketplace listings? or is there a partner seat/resell margin?
[04:40] Ethan Ward: flexible — hosted is usage-based per token. for partner-managed or dedicated offerings we do reserved capacity contracts and revenue share options. we can share partner program tiers.
[04:52] Alex Rivera: for marketplace listing we need an integration doc and an onboarding flow. do you have a self-serve connector?
[04:58] Jordan Lee: hi i'm jordan from partnerships — we have a partner onboarding kit and a marketplace API. typical flow: quick listing with hosted endpoints, then optional private listing for enterprise. i'll send the partner playbook.
[05:10] Priya Nair: network egress concerns — some customers are sensitive to token payload leaving region. can we pin region and ensure data residency?
[05:18] Maya Chen: yes, routing policies can pin by region, and private deployment keeps data on your infra. we'll document retention and delete policies too.
[05:26] Mark Delaney: what about multi-tenant isolation if we host a managed Redwood on our infra?
[05:30] Maya Chen: when running on your infra we still run tenant isolation at runtime — process isolation, per-tenant KV cache namespaces, and RBAC. for higher assurance we'd recommend dedicated pools per customer.
[05:44] Alex Rivera: ok timeline question — if we start a pilot how fast can we get a bench and an initial marketplace listing?
[05:50] Ethan Ward: typical pilot: 2-4 weeks for a benchmark + 4-6 weeks to list with basic support. varies if legal/nda takes longer.
[05:58] Priya Nair: legal — we prefer an NDA before hands-on infra tests.
[06:02] Alex Rivera: agreed. we'll need an NDA and then a technical SOW for pilot scope.
[06:08] Ethan Ward: we'll send our NDA and partner SOW template.
[06:12] [longer section — technical Q&A and clarifications]
[06:20] Priya Nair: for the benchmark, does redwood need docker / nvidia driver access? we run cluster with curated drivers and can't allow random images.
[06:30] Maya Chen: we can use your base images and we only need access to load the runtime. we'll provide a minimal container spec. no root if you don't want it. driver versions: we'll share recommended drivers and fallback options.
[06:44] Mark Delaney: i've seen some inference runtimes adopt kernel patches. do you require custom kernels or anything low-level?
[06:50] Maya Chen: no kernel patching required. we prefer standard drivers and some GPU tuning flags; heavier tuning optional but not mandatory for bench.
[06:58] Alex Rivera: on the business side — revenue split and support SLAs?
[07:05] Ethan Ward: partner splits are negotiable; we offer partner onboarding credits and co-marketing for early listings. SLAs depend on tier — dedicated customers can get uptime and latency SLOs.
[07:16] Sofia Morales: would you co-sell leads?
[07:19] Jordan Lee: yes co-sell is part of the program for qualified deals; we assign alliance manager and shared pipeline tracking.
[07:27] [noise/interruption — brief crosstalk] 
[07:36] Priya Nair: small detail — what's your observability surface? we need tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route dashboards.
[07:44] Maya Chen: all available — we have per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and alerts for regressions. we also integrate with common observability stacks (datadog, prometheus).
[07:58] Mark Delaney: good. for the pilot we'll want a small set of eval prompts to watch quality regressions. do you support eval hooks?
[08:04] Maya Chen: yes Redwood Optimize includes evals and quality monitoring, but we can run a simple eval harness as part of the pilot.
[08:14] Alex Rivera: last bit — procurement: what info do you need to get legal talking?
[08:20] Ethan Ward: i'll send our security pack, SOC2 report, sample MSA, and partner program terms. if you share your procurement template we can map gaps.
[08:30] Priya Nair: ok we'll share a topo doc and driver matrix.
[08:34] Ethan Ward: great. proposed bench steps: 1) NDA signed, 2) infra doc + sample data, 3) bench run (2-4 days), 4) results & cost estimates, 5) pilot statement of work.
[08:49] Alex Rivera: sounds good. any blockers today?
[08:52] Priya Nair: none aside from NDA and driver matrix.
[08:55] Maya Chen: noted. we'll prepare a lean bench plan so it's low friction.
[09:00] Jordan Lee: i'll include partner playbook and co-marketing options in the send.
[09:05] [recap and next steps]
[09:10] Ethan Ward: quick recap — ethan will send partner deck, security pack, and NDA link; maya will own bench plan & test harness; priya will share infra topology and gpu list; alex will coordinate legal. target dates — send materials by 2026-07-16 and bench the week of 2026-07-20. follow-up 2026-07-28 to review.
[09:35] Alex Rivera: yep good, thanks everyone. excited to move quickly.
[09:40] Mark Delaney: thanks — looking forward to the perf numbers.
[09:44] Ethan Ward: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
[46:40] Call ended
